observations: A 2014 primary study tested stable human dermal fibroblasts heterologously expressing mutated HLA-G1 with GFP.
The construct modified the endoplasmic-reticulum retrieval motif and 3′-UTR miRNA-binding sites; exact sequence changes were not reported in the abstract.

source_tools.relevance: Primary study design and construct modifications

entities.name: Human dermal fibroblasts
observations: Stable transgenic fibroblasts expressing mutated HLA-G1/GFP were compared with reported GFP fibroblast controls.
The abstract uses HDF-GFP for the PBMC assay and HDF-GDP for the NK assay comparator; HDF-GDP should not be silently interpreted as wild-type HLA-G1.

entities.name: Mutated HLA-G1
observations: Heterologous expression in human dermal fibroblasts reduced NK-cell-mediated cytolysis by 73% relative to the reported control.
The same construct reduced PHA-activated PBMC proliferation by 30% relative to HDF-GFP.
The abstract does not report a direct wild-type HLA-G1 arm or statistical significance values.

entities.name: mHLA-G1 reduces alloreactivity
observations: In vitro, mutated HLA-G1 expression in human dermal fibroblasts was associated with 73% lower NK-mediated cytolysis and 30% lower activated-PBMC proliferation versus reported controls.
No independent primary study was identified in the focused search; later literature reiterated the finding in review form.
